job_title: AI / ML & Full-Stack Software Engineer (Graduate / Entry-Level)
pool_summary: The pool separates into a small research-heavy AI cohort, a broader full-stack product-building cohort, and a few candidates with unusually strong academic or external-environment signals. The clearest upper-echelon differentiators are applied AI system complexity, independently owned end-to-end products, measurable validation or operational impact, and research or international depth beyond baseline coursework.

axes.label: Research-to-Application Depth
axes.rationale: For an entry-level Applied AI role, substantive research involvement is more differentiating than generic ML exposure, particularly when it connects to a novel method, publication, or real-world application. This separates candidates with sustained lab or research ownership from those whose evidence is limited to listed tools or one basic model.
axes.strong_criteria: Demonstrates active [action] ownership in a substantive AI research effort across at least one applied domain—such as LLMs, continual learning, computer vision, robotics, healthcare, or intelligent transportation—and provides a research artifact or verified research trajectory such as a peer-reviewed publication, funded lab project, multi-month research appointment, or novel evaluated method.
axes.moderate_criteria: Shows active [action] participation in one supervised AI research or lab project, such as training a classifier, processing research data, or implementing an applied ML prototype, but without a publication, sustained multi-domain trajectory, or clearly novel/evaluated contribution.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 4/10 candidates show strong or moderate evidence; approximately 2/10 show strong evidence.

axes.label: Applied AI System Complexity
axes.rationale: The job requires turning ML capability into production-oriented systems spanning retrieval, perception, signal processing, and model-serving workflows. The pool contains a meaningful but selective cluster with exposure to complex modalities and operational pipelines rather than isolated coursework models.
axes.strong_criteria: Provides active [action] ownership of a multi-stage AI system with meaningful architectural complexity—for example real-time computer vision plus recognition, OCR and document transformation, EEG or signal-processing authentication, continual-learning robotics, or hybrid semantic/lexical RAG—and explains the pipeline, evaluation, or deployment behavior.
axes.moderate_criteria: Actively [action] builds or evaluates a single applied model or AI component, such as an image classifier, URL classifier, recommendation model, or basic document-processing pipeline, but lacks evidence of multi-stage orchestration, real-time constraints, retrieval architecture, or deployment complexity.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 5/10 candidates show strong or moderate evidence; approximately 3/10 show strong evidence.

axes.label: End-to-End Product Ownership
axes.rationale: The role combines AI with full-stack product engineering, so the differentiator is not merely knowing React or Node but independently connecting interfaces, APIs, persistence, authentication, and user-facing workflows. This axis distinguishes candidates who have shipped coherent products from candidates with only tool lists or narrow frontend exposure.
axes.strong_criteria: Demonstrates active [action] ownership of at least one end-to-end product, including multiple layers such as frontend/mobile UI, backend APIs, database persistence, authentication or authorization, and a real workflow; evidence should include building from scratch, independently delivering a client application, or owning a substantial production-like feature.
axes.moderate_criteria: Shows active [action] delivery of a smaller full-stack or mobile application with at least two connected layers—such as a React/Flutter frontend plus REST backend and database—but with limited evidence of independent ownership, security/workflow depth, or complete product scope.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 5/10 candidates show strong or moderate evidence; approximately 2/10 show strong evidence.

axes.label: Measured Impact & Validation
axes.rationale: Quantified outcomes are unusually selective in this pool and are especially valuable for judging whether an entry-level candidate can validate engineering or model work rather than merely describe implementation. The observed evidence ranges from model accuracy to processing-time reduction and concurrent-user capacity.
axes.strong_criteria: Provides active [action] ownership of a system or model with a concrete validation or operational metric comparable to the pool’s strongest evidence: approximately 98% model accuracy, around 60% processing-time reduction, or a demonstrated real-time/concurrent-user workload around 100 users; the metric must be tied to the candidate’s implementation or evaluation method.
axes.moderate_criteria: Actively [action] builds, deploys, or evaluates an application or model with some stated testing, performance, accuracy, user, or workflow outcome, but below the observed high-water marks or without enough methodological detail to verify the result.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 2/10 candidates show strong evidence and approximately 4/10 show strong or moderate evidence.

axes.label: Academic & External Environment Signal
axes.rationale: Because all contenders share the same BS CS baseline, academic distinction and experience in selective or international environments provide a pool-relative signal of preparation and exposure to higher-bar work. This is intentionally separate from technical ownership: it measures the environment and verified academic trajectory, not the complexity of a candidate’s projects.
axes.strong_criteria: Has verified academic distinction around the upper end of this pool—approximately 3.6+ CGPA—and at least one additional external-environment signal such as an international exchange or university research placement, distinction during international study, or sustained work in a selective research lab or external technology organization.
axes.moderate_criteria: Has either a comparatively strong academic record around 3.4+ CGPA or a verified external environment such as a research lab, international collaboration, or technology-company placement, but not both at the upper-pool level.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 5/10 candidates show strong or moderate evidence; approximately 2/10 show strong evidence.
